Method

Edition status at this 12 November authoring receipt: prelaunch, bounded 416-identity eligible core frozen, archive not_published, DOI null and no published edition history. The proposed first edition is research-2026-11-12.1, edition date 12 November 2026, with the actual captured-source cutoff 2026-11-12T17:32:13.289438Z. A date and release identity do not establish publication. The first actual edition is intended as soon as all existing research, source, review, audit, privacy and technical gates pass under the authorized one-time launch calendar. Later comprehensive editions target Monday 09:00 America/Los_Angeles with the preceding Friday 17:00 captured-source cutoff. Daily preparation targets 16:00 Pacific. No capture, review or publication is backdated.

Method

The weekly change unit is a versioned source-supported claim, not an increase in word count or an older paper newly encountered by the research team. Source publication date, described event date, capture timestamp, assertion as-of date, review timestamp and edition publication date remain separate. A capture performed on 9 November in Los Angeles may be dated 10 November UTC. It does not retroactively satisfy a 6 November cutoff. Later independent review can approve the captured content without changing the time at which the document was captured.

Method

This authoring refresh extends the actual e55-reviewed unpublished input of 2,292 approved assertions, 225 reviewed paper works, 73 qualifying supplier groups, 68 dataset families and 47 benchmark families to the final selected input of 2,548 approved assertions, the same 225 reviewed works and 73 supplier groups, 85 dataset families and 87 benchmark families. Seventeen dataset and forty benchmark families add 57 substantive atlas entries; these include the five reasoning-distillation families and 52 further families. The full twelve chapters, nine stable executive finding IDs, ten original pilot identities, supplier dossiers and reviewed-work bibliography are retained. Exact unchanged paragraphs are preserved and every changed or added block is inventoried for new synthesis review. Counts describe approved source coverage and identity dispositions, not contemporaneous news, an automatically improved method or a new published weekly edition.

Source-backed finding

The commercial event dates illustrate why review time must not become news time. Labelbox’s financing announcement is dated 14 October 2026; Proximal’s annualized-revenue announcement is dated 29 September 2026; Mercor’s 25 June investigation account describes a March 2026 LiteLLM incident. Their inclusion in this newly expanded preparation does not make them November events. The financing, annualization and incident qualifications remain part of the respective evidence records.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing, repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure, candidate.supplier.mercor.incident

Method

The earlier initial calculation counted FineWeb-Edu as a separate family. Current identity review treats it as a FineWeb subset release, so current coverage counts one FineWeb family. The earlier frozen files retain their original exact bytes. The correction is an explicit change in identity accounting, not a disappearance of the educational subset or a retraction of its documented model-scoring workflow. Future change logs should report family identity corrections separately from newly added source observations.

Research gap

No prior published edition exists in this ledger, so a week-over-week market trend is not estimable from these records. The first publishable comparison will need an actual frozen predecessor, a current source cutoff, a claim-level change list and disclosure of whether each change is a new event, a newly captured older source, a corrected scope or a reclassified identity. Scheduled dates, package preparation and website visibility should be reported separately from archive confirmation.

Method

Correction accounting preserves original assertions and their actual prior positive/negative review history. The current report assesses 141 affected paragraphs with 370 stale binding occurrences and five affected executive findings; these resolve through 84 distinct approved successors. Some statements remain scientifically supported with narrowed qualifications, while others require explicit wording changes: DAYJOB healthcare and finance time bases differ, Snorkel timing is acceptance- and project-conditioned, TrustScale’s rebrand evidence is decoded application-bundle text, and paper-only APEX-Accounting counts are separate from a captured leaderboard conflict. Original APTO, Magpie, OpenAssistant and Dataocean scope restrictions remain. These changes neither relabel prior diagnostics nor complete the formal launch audits.
